hook: I almost didn't buy the $299 robot mop. Here's why I did.

scenes.visual_prompt: Person standing in kitchen staring skeptically at a mop and bucket, arms crossed
scenes.on_screen_text: I was skeptical of the $299 price
scenes.voiceover: A self-washing, self-emptying robot for $299 sounded too good, so I checked the pricing history.

scenes.visual_prompt: Graphic timeline showing $1,000-$1,300 in 2023 shrinking down to $299 in 2026
scenes.voiceover: The same self-cleaning dock mechanism cost three to four times as much eighteen months ago.

scenes.visual_prompt: Comparison chart graphic: premium camera navigation vs simpler obstacle mapping on a budget unit
scenes.voiceover: What got stripped out is premium navigation — fewer cameras, simpler obstacle mapping. Not the wash-and-empty mechanism.

scenes.visual_prompt: Robot vacuum mapping a clean open-plan kitchen and living room in a single pass, LiDAR beam graphic
scenes.voiceover: These units are built for open hard-floor layouts — kitchens, living rooms, hallways.

scenes.visual_prompt: Robot vacuum struggling slightly against thick carpet pile in a heavily-carpeted bedroom
scenes.voiceover: Heavy-carpet homes see a lot less benefit from this specific feature set.

scenes.visual_prompt: Calendar graphic showing Black Friday through early December with price staying flat
scenes.voiceover: This pricing tends to hold through early December, not just spike on the one day — so you're not racing a clock.

scenes.visual_prompt: Clean kitchen floor, robot docked, person relaxed on couch, link icon overlay
scenes.on_screen_text: My full verdict is on the blog
scenes.voiceover: My full verdict — including who should skip this — is linked in my bio.

caption: I went in skeptical of a $299 self-washing robot mop. The price history checks out, but it's not for every floor plan. Full verdict — including who should actually wait — linked in bio.
